narrative.overview:
ConstructOps surfaces are built like a contractor's plan set: a cool paper sheet, a visible drafting grid, ruled schedules, a title block that carries the tenant's identity, and revision marks reserved for change. The product is a quiet instrument; the tenant is the author. ConstructOps never puts its own identity on a tenant surface.

This is a working document, not a brochure. The landing page lets a visitor's answers draft an itemized quote on the spot. The app compresses projects, money, and approvals into dense, legible schedules. The portal gives one client their job, its change orders, and a stamped signed record. Across all three, the material is paper, ink, and type; the hierarchy comes from rules and scale, not decoration.
keyCharacteristics: Cool paper ground, white working sheets, near-black ink.
Square corners and hard 1px rules; the only curve is a radio indicator.
Archivo drives hierarchy; Saira Stencil appears only on sheet numbers and stamps.
Tenant color enters through computed brand variables, never through product chrome.
Revision red and the stamp are scarce, meaningful signals.
Motion behaves like drafting: rows appear, dimension lines draw, a stamp lands.

rules.name: The Tenant Ink Rule
rules.body: Tenant color is data, not product identity. Product chrome stays paper and ink; tenant color appears only through brand variables on actions and title blocks.

rules.name: The Revision Rarity Rule
rules.body: Revision red means change or danger. It is not an accent for emphasis, decoration, or ordinary links. If nothing changed, nothing should be red.

rules.name: The Computed Foreground Rule
rules.body: Never hand-pick a foreground on a tenant color. Foregrounds come from the contrast policy: 4.5:1 for body text, 3:1 for large text and graphics.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: Any number a reader might compare uses tabular numerals and the data treatment. Money is right-aligned in schedules.

rules.name: The Two-Family Rule
rules.body: Archivo and Saira Stencil only. No third family; no monospace as body copy.

rules.name: The Sheet Rule
rules.body: Content sits on a sheet, and a sheet has edges. Do not float text on unbounded gradient fields or let a table escape its border.

rules.name: The One-Scroll Rule
rules.body: The document scrolls vertically; a dense table may scroll horizontally inside its own sheet. The page never gains a horizontal scrollbar.

rules.name: The Flat-by-Default Rule
rules.body: If a surface can be understood from its border and paper tone, it gets no shadow. Blurred shadows are not a hierarchy tool.

rules.name: The Hard-Offset Rule
rules.body: A hard offset shadow must be earned by a single physical object on a marketing surface. It never appears on ordinary app cards, inputs, or tables.

rules.name: The Square-Sheet Rule
rules.body: No rounded cards, pill buttons, or soft input corners. If a container feels too plain, add a rule or change the type scale, not a radius.

rules.name: The One-Circle Rule
rules.body: The only circular geometry is the radio indicator. Avatars, badges, and status dots stay square.

rules.name: The Control Contract
rules.body: Every control is at least 44px tall, has a visible 2px ink focus ring with a 2px paper offset, and uses the same press treatment.

rules.name: The Status-Only Badge Rule
rules.body: Badges communicate state, not decoration. If an item has no state, it gets no badge.

dos: Do ground every page on cool paper and place working content on white sheets.
Do use one display title per page, followed by a label that names the surface.
Do use 1px ink rules and dotted control-line rules to structure dense information.
Do reserve revision red and the stamp for actual change, rejection, or destruction.
Do compute tenant foregrounds with the contrast policy and show the result in /system.
Do keep numbers tabular, money right-aligned, and comparisons scannable.
Do let wide schedules scroll inside their sheet while the document stays vertically honest.
Do move with transform and opacity only; respect prefers-reduced-motion with instant states.
donts: Don't round cards, buttons, inputs, or badges. The radio indicator is the only circle.
Don't add blueprint texture, torn paper, tape, fake photography, or decorative gradients. The drafting grid is the only pattern.
Don't use revision red as a decorative accent or to emphasize ordinary copy.
Don't put ConstructOps branding on a tenant surface; the tenant is the author.
Don't stack blurred shadows or use elevation to fake hierarchy that rules can provide.
Don't introduce a third type family, script face, or monospace body copy.
Don't use pill-shaped status chips or circular avatars.
Don't let a table widen the page or hide its overflow without an affordance.
